dimensions.assessment: Affects members of the Armed Forces, Department of Defense civilian personnel, veterans, and their primary next of kin.
dimensions.evidence: every member of the Armed Forces who dies or is wounded in hostilities is entitled to be counted... in the casualty records

dimensions.assessment: Ensures accurate casualty accounting and restores deployment-related benefits, awards, special pay, leave, and tax authorities that might otherwise be altered by administrative reclassifications.
dimensions.evidence: no false assertion that hostilities have ceased nor arbitrary termination... may be used to deny servicemembers... the benefits and awards they are due

dimensions.assessment: Restores financial, leave, and tax benefits associated with active contingency operations for eligible personnel, but does not specify an aggregate fiscal expenditure amount.
dimensions.evidence: benefits associated with special pay, leave, and tax authorities in titles 10, 37, and 5, United States Code

dimensions.assessment: Amends title 10 United States Code regarding definitions of contingency operations, casualty records, and deployment benefit eligibility protections.
dimensions.evidence: Section 101(a)(13) of title 10, United States Code, is amended

dimensions.assessment: Includes immediate one-time restoration actions for operations since February 28, 2026, alongside permanent statutory prohibitions on future administrative reclassifications.
dimensions.evidence: Not later than 30 days after the date of enactment of this Act, the Secretary of Defense shall restore all casualty records

missing_information: Total number of personnel affected and total financial cost of restored benefits.
importance_detail.rationale: Prohibits the Secretary of Defense from manipulatively reclassifying ongoing contingency operations or casualty records to conceal the human cost of war or alter deployment-related benefit eligibility. Requires restoration of casualty records and benefits related to Operation Fury since February 28, 2026.
